==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|emty}}, {{m|enm|amty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ǣmtiġ}}, {{m|ang|ǣmettiġ|t=vacant, empty, free, idle, unmarried|lit=without must or obligation, leisurely}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|-}} {{m|gem-pro|*uz-|t=out}} + {{der|en|gem-pro|*mōtijô}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtô|t=must, obligation, need}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtiþô|t=ability, accommodation}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*med-|t=measure; to acquire, possess, be in command}}. Related to {{m+|ang|ġeǣmtigian|t=to empty}}, {{m|ang|ǣmetta|t=leisure}}, {{m|ang|mōtan|t=can, to be allowed}}. More at [[mote]], [[meet]]. The [[interconsonantal]] [[excrescent]] ''p'' is a [[euphonic]] insertion{{R:Etymonline|empty}} dating from Middle English. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈɛm(p).ti/|[ˈɛm(p).tʰi]|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-empty.ogg|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-empty.ogg|a=US}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈɪm(p).ti/|[ˈɪm(p).tʰi]|a=Southern US,AAVE,pin-pen}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈem(p).ti/|[ˈem(p).tʰi]|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛmpti|ɛmti|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|emp|ty}} ===Adjective=== [[File:In a empty guest room with a chihuahua.jpg|thumb|alt=A man seated in an elaborate chair in an empty room, with a chihuahua on his lap|A man and dog sitting in an '''empty''' room (1)]] {{en-adj|er}} # [[devoid|Devoid]] of [[content]]; containing nothing or nobody; [[vacant]]. #: {{syn|en|unoccupied|clear|leer|q3=obsolete|id3=empty|toom|q4=rare dialect|clean|q5=informal|Thesaurus:empty}} #: {{ant|en|full}} #: {{ux|en|an '''empty''' purse}} #: {{ux|en|an '''empty''' jug}} #: {{ux|en|an '''empty''' stomach}} #* {{RQ:Orwell Nineteen Eighty-Four|page=103|chapter=1|passage={{...}} something in the little man's appearance suggested that he would be sufficiently attentive to his own comfort to choose the '''emptiest''' table.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1970|author=Wilfrido D. Nolledo|title=But for the Lovers|publisher=Dalkey Archive Press|chapter=19|page=165|pageurl=https://books.google.ca/books?id=Uh2M3_2vOiUC&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false |passage={{...}} San Sebastian Church was desolate in the courtyard; '''emptier''', lonelier inside with its pews stretched out like fallen pylons varnished by dolorous residue. From each candlelit nook stared in stony despair one after another saint, regal and rueful: proffering forgiveness, peace, ''a todo''.}} #* {{quote-web|en |date=2011-10-23 |author=Phil McNulty |title=Man Utd 1 - 6 Man City |work=w:BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15325536.stm |page= |passage=United's stature is such that one result must not bring the immediate announcement of a shift in the balance of power in Manchester - but the swathes of '''empty''' seats around Old Trafford and the wave of attacks pouring towards David de Gea's goal in the second half emphasised that City quite simply have greater firepower and talent in their squad at present.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120124231543/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15325536.stm|archivedate=24 January 2012}} # {{lb|en|computing|programming|mathematics}} Containing no [[element]]s (as of a [[string]], [[array]], or [[set]]), opposed to being [[null]] (having no valid value). #: {{ant|en|non-empty}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Free; clear; devoid; often with ''of''. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Love's Labour's Lost|act=V|scene=ii|page=144|passage=And I ſhal finde you '''emptie''' of that fault,
Right ioyfull of your reformation.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=XI|lines=614-617|passage=For that fair femal Troop thou sawst, that seemd
Of Goddesses, so blithe, so smooth, so gay,
Yet '''empty''' of all good wherein consists
Womans domestic honour and chief praise;|year=1873}} # Having nothing to carry, [[emptyhanded]]; unburdened. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=23|passage=I hope our Ladies treaſure and our owne,
May ſerue for ranſome to our liberties:
Returne our Mules and '''emptie''' Camels backe,
That we may trauell into ''Siria'', {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Timon of Athens|act=III|scene=vi|page=89|passage=I hope it remaines not vnkindly with your Lordſhip, that I return'd you an '''empty''' Meſſenger.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|3|21|passage=And I will giue this people fauour in the sight of the Egyptians, and it shall come to passe that when ye goe, ye shall not goe '''empty''':}} # Destitute of effect, sincerity, or sense; said of language. #: {{coi|en|'''empty''' words, or threats}} #: {{coi|en|'''empty''' offer}} #: {{coi|en|'''empty''' promises}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1697|author=w:Colley Cibber|title=Woman's Wit|section=act V|page=190|url=https://archive.org/details/dramaticworksofc01cibbuoft |passage={{...}} words are but '''empty''' thanks; my future conduct best will speak my gratitude.}} # Unable to satisfy; hollow; vain. #: {{ux|en|'''empty''' pleasures}} #* {{RQ:Pope Windsor Forest|year=1713|page=18|passage=Ev'n I more sweetly pass my careless days,
Pleas'd in the silent shade with '''empty''' praise;}} # Destitute of reality, or real existence; unsubstantial. #: {{ux|en|'''empty''' dreams}} # Destitute of, or lacking, sense, knowledge, or courtesy. #: {{ux|en|'''empty''' brains}} #: {{ux|en|an '''empty''' coxcomb}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|act=II|scene=vii|page=203|column=2|passage=Art thou thus bolden'd man by thy diſtres?
Or elſe a rude deſpiſer of good manners,
That in ciuility thou ſeem'ſt ſo '''emptie'''?}} # {{lb|en|of some female animals, especially cows and sheep}} Not [[pregnant]]; not producing offspring when expected to do so during the breeding season. #: {{ux|en|'''Empty''' cow rates have increased in recent years.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|of a plant or tree}} Producing nothing; [[unfruitful]]. #: {{ux|en|an '''empty''' vine}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|41|27|passage={{...|And the seuen thin and ill fauoured kine that came vp after them, are seuen yeeres:}} and the seuen '''emptie''' eares blasted with the East wind{{...|, shall bee seuen yeeres of famine.}}}} # [[hungry|Hungry]]. # {{lb|en|oenology}} Lacking between the onset of tasting and the [[finish]]. #: {{syn|en|hollow}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1993|author=Robert M. Parker|title=Parker's Wine Buyer's Guide|page=967 |passage=Grotesquely vegetal, excessively oaked, '''empty''' wines were routinely produced in the mid-1980s.
